ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In rectangle $ABCD$, where $AB=5$ and $BC=5\sqrt{3}$, point $P$ is a moving point on $BC$. Connect $AP$ and construct an equilateral triangle $APE$ with $AP$ as one of its sides. Connect $DE$. What is the minimum value of segment $DE$ as point $P$ moves?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct an equilateral triangle ABF with AB as its side, draw a line connecting FE, and draw line DH perpendicular to the extension of FE at point H, as shown in the figure,\\
since quadrilateral ABCD is a rectangle, it follows that $\angle ABP=\angle BAD=90^\circ$,\\
since $\triangle APE$ and $\triangle ABF$ are equilateral triangles, it follows that $\angle BAF=\angle PAE=60^\circ$, $BA=FA$, PA=AE, thus $\angle BAP=\angle FAE$,\\
therefore $\triangle BAP\cong \triangle FAE$, hence $\angle ABP=\angle AFE=90^\circ$,\\
since $\angle FAG=90^\circ-60^\circ=30^\circ$, it follows that $\angle AGE=90^\circ-30^\circ=60^\circ$,\\
since AB=AF=5, it follows that $AG=AF\div\cos30^\circ=\frac{10\sqrt{3}}{3}$,\\
therefore, point E moves on the ray FH, since AD=BC=$5\sqrt{3}$, it follows that DG=AD−AG=$\frac{5\sqrt{3}}{3}$,\\
since DH is perpendicular to FE, $\angle AGE=\angle HGD=60^\circ$, it follows that $DH=DG\times \sin60^\circ=\frac{5}{2}$,\\
also, since the perpendicular segment is the shortest, it follows that when point E coincides with point H, DE has its minimum value, and the minimum value is $\boxed{\frac{5}{2}}$.

Since $\triangle APE$ and $\triangle ABF$ are equilateral triangles, it follows that $\angle BAF=\angle PAE=60^\circ$, $BA=FA$, $PA=AE$, thus $\angle BAP=\angle FAE$. Therefore $\triangle BAP\cong \triangle FAE$, hence $\angle ABP=\angle AFE=90^\circ$. Since $\angle FAG=90^\circ-60^\circ=30^\circ$, it follows that $\angle AGE=90^\circ-30^\circ=60^\circ$. Since $AB=AF=5$, it follows that $AG=AF\div\cos 30^\circ=\frac{10\sqrt{3}}{3}$. Therefore, point $E$ moves on the ray $FH$. Since $AD=BC=5\sqrt{3}$, it follows that $DG=AD-AG=\frac{5\sqrt{3}}{3}$. Since $DH$ is perpendicular to $FE$, $\angle AGE=\angle HGD=60^\circ$, so $DH=DG\times \sin 60^\circ=\frac{5}{2}$. Also, since the perpendicular segment is the shortest, it follows that when point $E$ coincides with point $H$, $DE$ has its minimum value, and the minimum value is $\boxed{\frac{5}{2}}$.
